# X (Twitter) connector

Go connector for the X API v2, focused on posting and managing tweets for a business account: create/delete tweets, timelines, mentions, recent search, likes and reposts. Generated from a curated OpenAPI spec authored from the official X documentation.

## How to use this connector

One `Client` serves one X account. It needs an OAuth 2.0 **user-context**
access token (authorization-code + PKCE flow, scopes `tweet.read
tweet.write users.read`, plus `like.write` for likes) for posting; an
app-only bearer token works for reads only:

```go
import (
    "github.com/pax-beehive/connector"
    "github.com/pax-beehive/connector/x"
)

c, err := x.NewClient(&x.Config{AccessToken: "..."})

// Post a tweet.
resp, err := c.CreateTweet(ctx, &x.CreateTweetRequest{
    Text: connector.Ptr("Hello world"),
})
// Reply / quote / poll:
//   Reply: &x.TweetReply{InReplyToTweetId: connector.Ptr("...")}
//   QuoteTweetId: connector.Ptr("...")
//   Poll: &x.TweetPoll{Options: []string{"a","b"}, DurationMinutes: connector.Ptr(60)}

me, err := c.GetMe(ctx, &x.GetMeRequest{UserFields: connector.Ptr("public_metrics")})
```

`LikeTweet`/`Retweet` operate on behalf of the authenticated user: the
`Id` path param must be the authenticated user's own ID (from `GetMe`).

## Auth model

- Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer <AccessToken>`.
- Tokens are NOT auto-refreshed; run the OAuth refresh-token flow
  (`offline.access` scope) outside this SDK.

## Errors

Non-2xx responses become `*connector.APIError`. `Code`/`Message` carry
the v2 problem `title`/`detail` (or the legacy numeric `code`/`message`,
e.g. 89 = invalid token). Rate limiting surfaces as HTTP 429.

## Data conventions

- GET endpoints return minimal objects unless you list extra fields in
  `TweetFields`/`UserFields`/`MediaFields` (comma-separated) and request
  related objects via `Expansions`.
- `StartTime`/`EndTime` are RFC3339 UTC strings, e.g.
  `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- Pagination: pass `Meta.NextToken` back as `PaginationToken`
  (`NextToken` for search).

## Capability boundaries (what this connector does NOT do)

- No OAuth flow: obtaining/refreshing tokens happens outside this SDK.
- No media upload: `TweetMedia.MediaIds` must come from an upload done
  elsewhere (the chunked upload endpoint is not covered).
- No DMs, Spaces, Lists, streaming, or full-archive search.
- No retries by default; opt in with `connector.WithRetry` (HTTP 429
  honors `Retry-After`).

### Client options (all connectors)

`NewClient(cfg, opts...)` accepts shared options from the root
`connector` package:

- `connector.WithTimeout(d)` — overall per-call deadline (covers retries).
- `connector.WithRetry(connector.RetryPolicy{})` — opt-in automatic
  retries with exponential backoff honoring `Retry-After`. Defaults:
  3 attempts, statuses 429/502/503/504; non-idempotent methods (POST) are
  retried only on 429 unless `RetryNonIdempotent` is set.
- `connector.WithHTTPClient(hc)` — custom `*http.Client`.

### Error handling (all connectors)

Every non-2xx response is a `*connector.APIError` (StatusCode, service
Code/Message, raw Body, and the server's `RetryAfter` hint). Classify
without unwrapping via `connector.IsRateLimited(err)` (429),
`IsUnauthorized` (401), `IsForbidden` (403), `IsNotFound` (404),
`IsServerError` (5xx), `IsRetryable` (429/502/503/504), or use
`connector.AsAPIError(err)` / `connector.StatusCode(err)`.

Anything not listed here is outside this connector's capability boundary.

- `Retweet` — `POST /2/users/{id}/retweets`
- `UnlikeTweet` — `DELETE /2/users/{id}/likes/{tweet_id}`
- `Unretweet` — `DELETE /2/users/{id}/retweets/{source_tweet_id}`
